annotation.title_clean: Chair's summary – Second 2024 session of the GGE on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems
annotation.title_en: Chair's summary – Second 2024 session of the GGE on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Chairperson of the CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS (H.E. Robert in den Bosch, Netherlands)
annotation.summary_en: Chair's informal summary of the August 2024 CCW Group of Governmental Experts session on lethal autonomous weapons systems. It records discussion of the Chair's rolling text: characterization of LAWS, application of IHL, a two-tier prohibition/regulation approach, risk mitigation and accountability, and the divergent state positions on a new binding instrument.
key_provisions_or_claims: Rolling text characterizes LAWS as systems that select and engage targets without further human intervention after activation; 'lethal' and 'nominal human input' remain contested.
Two-tier approach: prohibit LAWS incompatible with IHL, regulate others via limits on targets, duration, scope and engagements.
Humans must remain accountable for use-of-force decisions; accountability cannot be transferred to machines.
Risk mitigation: testing, Article 36 legal reviews, bias and automation-bias measures.
Divided views on new binding instrument (Protocol VI) versus existing IHL sufficiency; mandate deadline is 2026.
